findings.body: The test claims to assert "the wire between config and gateway," but it constructs `GatewayModel` directly (bypassing `from_config`) and calls `reasoning_options` on a field it just set — it never calls `harness()` or verifies that `with_default_provider_options` receives the value. If a future change drops the `reasoning_effort: models.reasoning_effort.clone()` line in `from_config`, this test still passes. The test gives false confidence about exactly the failure mode its comment warns about: a setting that is read and documented but never forwarded.
findings.title: Configured-effort test does not exercise the gateway wire

value.summary: The change replaces a hard-coded reasoning-disable with a configurable `reasoning_effort` field, wiring it through `reasoning_options` into `with_default_provider_options`. The logic is sound: "off" and empty strings disable reasoning, any other trimmed value is passed through as an effort level. One test claims to verify the config-to-gateway wire but only re-tests `reasoning_options` in isolation, leaving the actual forwarding path unexercised.
